title: A Performance-Portable MultiGPU Implementation of 3D Euler Equations using ProtoX and IRIS
problem: Computational scientists face challenges developing and optimizing code for heterogeneous HPC systems with multiple GPUs while maintaining performance portability across different GPU architectures.
motivation: Modern HPC facilities comprise heterogeneous GPU nodes, creating demand for performance-portable solutions that efficiently run computational kernels across AMD and NVIDIA GPUs without extensive platform-specific optimization.
method: ProtoX uses two tools to automatically generate optimized GPU programs: Proto provides the high-level structure for equations on regular grids, and SPIRAL generates efficient low-level code. These create kernels (specialized GPU programs) that solve Euler equations (equations describing fluid flow) using a high-accuracy method (fourth-order finite volume). IRIS, a runtime scheduling system, then distributes these kernels across multiple GPUs and optimizes them through two techniques—fusing operations into computation graphs (DAG fusion) and merging separate GPU tasks—enabling efficient execution on any GPU type.
key_novelty: Combining automatic GPU code generation for structured-grid equations with intelligent runtime fusion of computation operations (DAG and task fusion) enables the same code to run efficiently on different GPU architectures.
contributions: Performance-portable multiGPU implementation of 3D Euler equations via ProtoX and IRIS integration
Demonstration of ProtoX kernel generation for computational fluid dynamics on structured grids
Exploration of DAG fusion and task fusion optimizations in IRIS runtime for multiGPU efficiency
Empirical performance comparison across AMD Frontier and NVIDIA DGX-1 architectures
